headline: SAUDI ARABIA UNVEILS 110MT RARE EARTH-URANIUM FIND AT IAEA — 4TH LARGEST GLOBALLY, MA'ADEN+MP MATERIALS TO DEVELOP
snippet: Saudi Arabia's Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman announced the Jabal Sayid discovery at the IAEA General Conference on September 17, 2026 — a 110-114 million tonne ore deposit in the Madinah region containing an estimated 552,000 tonnes of heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium), 355,000 tonnes of light rare earths (neodymium, praseodymium), and 31,000 tonnes of uranium, ranking fourth globally by critical mineral resource value; the announcement follows a July 2026 US-Saudi civilian nuclear cooperation agreement and a partnership between Ma'aden and US-listed MP Materials for rare earth processing and uranium production.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD & SILVER DRILLS 654.7 G/T AG + 1.5% CU OVER 20.5M AT COSALA — BEST GRADE-WIDTHS IN MINE'S HISTORY
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA) released September 17, 2026 infill drilling results from the San Rafael, 120 Upper, and 120 Lower deposits at the Cosalá Complex in Sinaloa, Mexico — hole SR583 returned 654.7 g/t Ag and 1.5% Cu over a true width of 20.5 metres, located 30 metres outside the current 2025 Inferred Resource boundary, and a second hole returned 409.3 g/t Ag and 0.8% Cu over 14.1 metres true width; management described these as some of the best grade-thickness combinations drilled to date at any of the three zones, pointing to a meaningful resource update ahead.

headline: OSISKO METALS SPINS OUT $100M CRITICAL MINERALS VEHICLE — 645KM² NEW BRUNSWICK PORTFOLIO GETS STANDALONE ENTITY
snippet: Osisko Metals announced September 17, 2026 that its wholly-owned subsidiary Osisko Critical Minerals Corporation has launched a C$100.5 million private placement of special warrants at $0.25 per warrant to fund standalone exploration of a 645 km² New Brunswick critical minerals portfolio comprising 2,972 mineral claim units across three option agreements executed in 2026; the spinout frees Osisko Metals to focus exclusively on expanding the past-producing Gaspé Copper deposit in Québec, with Osisko Critical Minerals expected to operate as an independent public entity following closing on or about November 17, 2026.

headline: NORSEMONT DRILLS 41M AT 4.59 G/T AU IN CHILE — 18M AT 9.7 G/T BRECCIA MARKS BEST INTERVAL YET AT CHOQUELIMPIE
snippet: Norsemont Mining (CSE: NOM) released September 17, 2026 Phase 3 assays from the Vizcacha Zone at its 100%-owned Choquelimpie gold-silver-copper project in northern Chile — standout hole DD13 intersected 41 metres at 4.59 g/t Au, including 18 metres at 9.7 g/t Au hosted in altered hydrothermal breccia, the highest grade-thickness interval drilled in the program to date; sixteen holes for 4,100 metres have been completed in 2026 with Phase 3 focused on depth testing beyond the 2025 resource boundary, and additional assays from the remaining holes are pending.

headline: TRIDENT HITS 31.98 G/T AU OVER 3M AT 220M BELOW HISTORIC WORKINGS — CONTACT LAKE DEEP DRILL OPENS NEW FLOOR
snippet: Trident Resources Corp. released September 17, 2026 the first assay results from its 2026 summer drill program at the Contact Lake Project in Saskatchewan's La Ronge Gold Belt — hole CL26050 returned 8.69 g/t Au over 11.97 metres from 613–625 metres depth, including 31.98 g/t Au over 3.16 metres, located 220 vertical metres below the deepest historical mine workings; the past-producing Contact Lake mine ran at a 6.16 g/t Au average head grade during its 1994–1998 operating life, and the program has now surpassed 11,000 metres of its planned 20,000 metres with assays from further holes pending.

headline: AMERICAN TUNGSTEN PASSES 30,000FT AT IDAHO IMA MINE — VEIN SYSTEM CONFIRMED BEYOND HISTORIC WORKINGS, RESTART STUDIED
snippet: American Tungsten (TSXV: TUNG) announced September 17, 2026 it has surpassed 30,000 feet of cumulative drilling at the IMA Mine in Lemhi County, Idaho — results confirm high-grade tungsten in the No.5 through No.7 vein array and validate the historic 41R vein in zones extending beyond previously mined areas, with the company simultaneously advancing engineering studies toward a potential underground mining restart; the announcement arrives days after the U.S. Department of War committed $450 million to rebuild the domestic tungsten supply chain, underscoring the strategic significance of a producing American source.

headline: CADILLAC MINES CLOSES LARDER DEAL FROM PAN AMERICAN SILVER — 1.3MOZ HISTORIC GOLD AT ABITIBI'S CADILLAC BREAK
snippet: Cadillac Mines Corporation (TSX: CADY) completed September 15, 2026 the acquisition of Pan American Silver's Larder Property — comprising 6,400 hectares and three gold deposits (Bear, Cheminis, Fernland) with 388,000 oz Indicated and 933,000 oz Inferred historical gold resource along the Larder Lake Cadillac Break — in exchange for 15 million Cadillac Mines shares; Pan American now holds approximately 6% of Cadillac and the transaction grows Cadillac's Abitibi land package to over 27,000 contiguous hectares adjacent to the historically significant Kerr-Addison property.

headline: ALBEMARLE DROPS 3.51% AS FED HIKE HITS LITHIUM EQUITIES — CATL JIANXIAWO SUPPLY DISRUPTION LIMITS DOWNSIDE
snippet: Lithium mining equities split on September 16–17, 2026, with Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) slumping 3.51% while SQM posted a more modest 0.88% decline as the Fed's first rate hike since 2023 rippled through interest-rate-sensitive growth stocks; the sell-off was partially contained by an ongoing production disruption at CATL's Jianxiawo mine in China — the world's largest lithium mine by capacity representing roughly 4% of global supply — while lithium carbonate in China slipped to a one-month low of CNY 143,000 per tonne as ample Australian spodumene supply continues to pressure pricing.

headline: GOLDSEEK: RATE HIKE IS A SIDESHOW — $2 TRILLION DEFICIT EACH YEAR IS THE REAL DRIVER OF THE GOLD BULL
snippet: A GoldSeek opinion piece published September 16, 2026 argues that investor obsession with the Fed's 25-basis-point rate hike misses the structural driver of gold's bull market — U.S. federal spending running more than $2 trillion over revenues annually regardless of the rate environment, with Treasury issuance continuously absorbing savings that would otherwise reach productive investment; the author contends gold investors should welcome higher rates as confirmation of fiscal credibility concerns rather than fearing them as traditional headwinds, since real yields have failed to restrain gold since central bank buying began dominating the market.

headline: FIRST MINING GOLD PRICES $50M BOUGHT DEAL AT $0.84 — SPRINGPOLE AND DUPARQUET ADVANCED ON FRESH CAPITAL
snippet: First Mining Gold Corp. (TSX: FF) announced September 17, 2026 an agreement with Haywood Securities, ATB Cormark Capital Markets, and National Bank Financial to sell 59.53 million common shares at $0.84 each for gross proceeds of C$50 million — net proceeds will advance the Springpole gold project in northwestern Ontario and the Duparquet project in Québec toward feasibility-stage milestones; the transaction demonstrates that the window for junior gold equity raises at premium valuations remains open despite this week's Fed rate hike.
